summary: Gradual rise in 5xx across streaming + generation routes coincident with cross-AZ peering degradation
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-14 12:10 UTC we observed a gradual increase in 5xx responses across both streaming and non-streaming generation endpoints for a subset of dedicated tenants (notably NimbleDocs). The error rate rose from baseline ~0.3% to ~6% over ~40 minutes. Impact: customer-facing errors (502/503/504) and increased tail latency; production traffic for the tenant experienced elevated timeouts and several runtime restarts. Environment: prod us-west-2 dedicated pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send sustained mixed traffic (chat + embeddings) at medium concurrency (10-20 concurrent sessions) to tenant-specific routes; 2) Observe increased hedged retries and upstream 5xx; 3) Check runtime /api/stats and apigw logs for retry amplification. Observed logs: api-gateway showed increased upstream 502/503 and retry loops; serving runtime logs show repeated kv-cache prefetch timeouts and occasional OOM_kill on ephemeral workers; network metrics show packet loss spikes on the cross-AZ peering link between us-west-2a and us-west-2b. Key timestamps: 12:08 UTC slight packet loss begin, 12:15 UTC apigw 5xx rate begins rising, 12:40 UTC peak 5xx ~6%.
investigation_notes: Initial correlation points: packet loss on cross-AZ peering (platform network telemetry) correlates with latency to NVMe-backed KV cache shard leaders used heavily during prefetch. Hypothesis A: intermittent peering degradation caused increased RPC latency to kv shard leaders, causing prefetch timeouts and holding KV locks longer; this amplified hedged retries at apigw which overloaded runtimes and triggered OOM_kill on ephemeral workers. Hypothesis B: a recent kernel update on a subset of dedicated hosts increased softirq latency under packet loss leading to slower reclaim and runtime thread stalls. Evidence: 1) p95 socket latencies to kv service increased from 12ms->220ms during window; 2) runtime process OOM events timestamp aligned with apigw retry spike; 3) netstats show briefly elevated retransmits and MTU mismatch warnings on peering NICs. Temporary mitigations tried: reduced hedged retry multiplier for affected tenant routes, forced traffic away from us-west-2b to us-west-2c for the tenant, increased kv prefetch timeout from 150ms to 500ms for dedicated pool. Results: lowering retries and rerouting reduced 5xx to ~0.8% within 12 minutes. Ongoing checks: kernel logs for the cohort hosts, NVMe/IO wait metrics, peering provider ticket opened.
comments: 12:30 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer NimbleDocs reported intermittent generation failures. Elevated 5xx observed in tenant dashboard. Escalating to SRE.

12:42 UTC - SRE (Marco): Confirmed packet loss on peering link. Initiated reroute of tenant traffic to alternative AZ and reduced hedged retry multiplier for tenant routing config. Noted immediate drop in 5xx.
13:05 UTC - Obs (Jun): KV shard RPC latency spikes present; added temporary prefetch timeout bump. Monitoring for runtime stability.
13:45 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer notified of mitigation steps and observed improved success rate; asked to validate on their side. Customer confirmed lower error rate in their telemetry.
14:10 UTC - Network (Leila): Opened ticket with cloud provider for peering performance (ticket CP-88473). Investigating whether maintenance or noisy neighbor caused transient packet loss.
resolution_notes: Mitigation sequence: 1) Reduced hedged retry multiplier for affected tenant routes to avoid retry amplification. 2) Rerouted tenant traffic off the affected peering path to alternative AZs. 3) Increased kv-cache prefetch timeout and added backoff for prefetch locks. 4) Coordinated with cloud provider to investigate peering link packet loss. Outcome: 5xx returned to near-baseline (~0.6%) and runtime restarts stopped. No code change required. Long-term action items created to harden: better peering health detection, adaptive retry/backoff in apigw, and KV prefetch lock timeouts.
next_steps: 1) Network team to follow up with provider and share root cause (owner: Leila) - target 2026-03-18. 2) SRE to schedule kernel rollback test on staging cohort to validate Hypothesis B (owner: Marco) - ETA 2 days. 3) Product: evaluate default hedged retry configuration and publish recommended tenant tuning guide (owner: Priya) - ETA 1 week. 4) Add automated alerting rule for cross-AZ peering packet-loss correlated with KV RPC latency.
